phasing_details.phase_detail: New Infill, Plantroom and rooftop ductwork

subdivision_of_building:
Ground Floor - Emergency Department, Majors, RAFT, Resus, E-SDEC, ED X-ray, Childrens' ED.
First Floor - New Infill to the current maternity ward ED entrance.
Second Floor - roof area above areas affected by works plus energy centre roof.
description:
As part of the reconfiguration of the Emergency Department at Queens Hospital, Romford, the following works are proposed:
1. New Infill Area to the current Maternity Ward to form a new Main Entrance Area for the Emergency
Departments.
2. New Rooftop plantroom and chiller enclosure for the Emergency Department plus associated duct and pipe
runs with maintenance access pathways, handrails and lighting, duct step-overs, companion-way ladders
and edge protection.
3. Minor changes to the ground floor facade of the existing envelope of the Emergency Department- to infill the existing A&E entrance and create a limited number of new door/ window openings.
decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be commenced not later than three years from the date of this permission.
To comply with the requirements of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise than in complete accordance with the approved plans (as set out on page one of this decision notice).
For the avoidance of doubt and to ensure that the development is carried out as approved.

All materials and external finishes shall be carried out strictly in accordance with details shown on approved plans and supporting information provided unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.
To ensure that the development is of sufficiently high quality and integrates with the surrounding environment.

a)            If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the local planning authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this unsuspected contamination shall be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved.

b)           Following completion of the remediation works as mentioned in (a) above, a 'Verification Report' must be submitted demonstrating that the works have been carried out satisfactorily and remediation targets have been achieved.

Reason:        To ensure that any previously unidentified contamination found at the site is investigated and satisfactorily addressed in order to protect those engaged in construction and occupation of the development from potential contamination.

The scheme to control noise and vibration, as detailed in the noise report prepared by RBA Acoustics -Ref: 14859.RP01.PNA.0 dated 30 April 2026 submitted with this application, shall be implemented, as a minimum, before the hereby permitted plant and machinery first comes into use.
The equipment shall be retained and maintained in accordance with those specifications for the lifetime of the development  thereafter to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To protect the amenity of noise sensitive receptors from noise from mechanical plant.

Prior to the first use of the mechanical ventilation system, chillers, condensers, or any associated plant, the equipment shall be installed with appropriate anti-vibration isolation measures in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and details.

The installed plant and associated isolation measures shall thereafter be retained and maintained in accordance with those specifications for the lifetime of the development thereafter to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In the interests of safeguarding the amenity of neighbouring occupiers and to prevent noise and vibration disturbance, in accordance with the objectives of the Havering Local Plan 2016-2031.

Statement Required by Article 35(2) of the Town and Country Planning (Development Management) Order 2015: No significant problems were identified during the consideration of the application, and therefore it has been determined in accordance with paragraph 38 of the National Planning Policy Framework.
